 Versus

 Chhattisgarh.

 Raipur, District - Raipur, Chhattisgarh.

---- Respond (Cause-title taken from Case Information System) ____ For Appellant : Mr. Malay Shrivastava,
Advocate For Respondent No.1 : Mr. Raja Sharma, Advocate For Respondent/State : Mr. Shashank Thakur, Dy. A.G. Hon'ble Shri Justice Ramesh Sinha, Chief Justice Hon'ble Shri Justice Sachin Singh Rajput, Judge Order on Board Per Ramesh Sinha, Chief Justice 14.06.2024 1.
Heard Mr. Malay Shrivastava, learned counsel for the appellant.

Also heard Mr. Shashank Thakur,
Dy. A.G for the State/respondent and Mr. Raja Sharma, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.1.
2.

The present writ appeal is preferred against an order dated 29.11.2021 passed by the learned Single Judge in WP(C) No. 4070 of 2021 whereby the petition of the respondent No.1 was allowed and authority concerned i.e. respondent No.3 is directed to pass an order on the application filed by the petitioner for appointment of the advocate of his choice and fix the fees as may be considered appropriate by him.

3. The facts of the case, are that, the respondent No.1 is a member of scheduled tribe and he is the victim of the case registered as Crime No.131 of 2017 for the commission of offences under Sections 147, 148, 188, 294, 506, 323, 395, 427, 447, 448, 452, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 & 120-B of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3(2), 3(iv), 3(v) & 3(1)(da)(dha) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Sanjay Agrawal vs Vishnu Singh on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18481861/
1 Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

The case is registered as Special Criminal Case (under SC/ST Act) 1989/55 of 2021 before the Special Court Baikunthpur, District Korea and has moved an application under Rule 4(5) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Rules, 1995 to engage advocate Mr. Arvind Singh after obtaining due consent from him.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Rules, 1995
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The learned Single Judge in WP(C) No. 4070 of 2021 favoured the petition of the respondent No.1 by allowing the same and authority concerned i.e. respondent No.3 is directed to pass an order on the application filed by the petitioner for appointment of the advocate of his choice and fix the fees as may be considered appropriate by him.

On contrary appellant in the present appeal submitted that Mr. Arvind Singh is continuously appearing on behalf of the respondent No.1 and against the appellant/petitioner in so many proceedings is illegal and unfair.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that learned Single Judge passed the order dated 29.11.2021 in WP(C) No.4070/2021 without giving any opportunity of hearing to the appellant or the other accused persons of Crime No.131/2017 is contrary to the law and argued at length to set aside the said order by allowing this appeal.

5. On the other hand, learned State counsel opposed the argument advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant and submits the learned Single Judge has not erred in delivering the order and no interference is called for by this Court.

Mr. Raja Sharma, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.1 supports the impugned order and submits that the learned Single Judge has rightly justified that the District Magistrate has the power under Rule 4(5) of the Rules, 1995 to fix the fees remuneration for engagement of any eminent Senior Advocate of the choice of the victim whatever he may consider appropriate.
6. We have heard the counsel for the parties and perused the impugned order and other documents appended with this writ appeal.

7. Considering the submissions advanced by the learned counsel for the parties, perusing the impugned order, the material available on record, records of the writ petition and also considering the finding recorded by the learned Single Judge while deciding the writ petition, we are of the considered view that the learned Single Judge has not committed any illegality, irregularity or jurisdictional error warranting interference by this Court and there is no merit in the writ appeal.
8. Accordingly, the writ appeal being devoid of merit is liable to be and is hereby dismissed.
No cost(s).

Sd/- Sd/-
 (Sachin Singh Rajput) (Ramesh Sinha)
